REASONS FOR JUDGMENT

OF THE

HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE VICKERS

Counsel for the Plaintiff:           T.M.G. appearing in
person

Counsel for the Defendant:            Alison E.
MacLennan, Q.C.

Place and Date of Hearing:
Vancouver, B.C.

May 4 - 7, May 11
- 14,

May 19 - 22, May 25, May 27
- 29,

June 29 - 30, July 2 - 3,
1998

[
1
]       The action by TMG seeking relief under the
provisions

of the
Family Relations Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 128
and
the

divorce action brought by AAG were consolidated for the

purposes of trial.  The issues arising from both
proceedings

are as follows:

1.   Divorce order;

2.   Whether access to the children by TMG is
to

continue to be supervised;

3.   Whether there should be an order of joint

guardianship;

4.   Whether the order restraining removal of
the

children from the jurisdiction of the
court

should be continued;

5.   A declaration and division of family
assets;

and,

6.   Spousal maintenance.

[
2
]       The parties were married on May 23, 1983.  They

separated May 19, 1994.  There are three children of the

marriage, namely:

RMG, born March 6, 1984;

SMG, born May 31, 1985; and

DMG, born April 9, 1987.

[
3
]       The parties have lived separate and apart since
the

date of separation and there is no hope of
reconciliation.

There will be an order that they be divorced from each
other.

[
4
]       In May of 1994, TMG accused AAG of physical
assaults

on the children and sexual assaults on two of the
children.

AAG was served with an ex parte order of the Provincial
Court

on May 19, 1994 ordering him to vacate the family home at
573

St. Giles Road, West Vancouver and to refrain from
attending

the family property at 1141 Butterball Drive, Qualicum
Beach.

[
5
]       An ex parte order of this court was obtained by
AAG

during the morning of June 10, 1994.  By that order he
was

granted interim custody of the children and possession of
the

family home in West Vancouver.  The order was set aside
later

the same day and TMG was granted interim custody of the

children, exclusive possession of the family home in West

Vancouver and AAG was denied access to the children.

[
6
]       On June 15, 1994, Dohm J. made an order
granting AAG

supervised access of limited duration.  TMG and AAG were

ordered not to discuss with their children the
allegations

which had been made concerning them in the action.  In

addition, TMG and AAG were both restrained from removing
the

children from British Columbia.  The order restricting
movement

of the children was not varied after custody of the
children

was awarded to AAG.  Thus, AAG has been required to
consult

counsel to obtain a variation of the order whenever he
wanted

to take the children to visit his parents in Ontario or

vacation with them outside the province.

[
7
]       On August 26, 1994, after a five day trial on
interim

issues, Braidwood J., as he then was, concluded that TMG
was

"dependent upon alcohol and drugs and their use has
a serious

effect on her ability to supervise and raise her infant

children."  He made, in part, the following orders:

1.   Interim custody of the children was
granted to

AAG;

2.   TMG was denied access to the children
until the

beginning of December, 1994 when
supervised

access was to begin;

3.   AAG was ordered to pay $5,000 to TMG; and,

4.   TMG was to return to the family home in
West

Vancouver all of the articles she had
removed

except personal items of clothing and
toiletry,

the move to be paid for by AAG.

TMG v. AAG (26 August 1994), Vancouver F940350 (B.C.S.C).

[
8
]       In his reasons for judgment, Braidwood J. said
the

following at page 16:

I have read the transcript of Mrs. [G.]'s testimony

before the learned Provincial Court Judge and I make

a specific finding that it is untrue in its entirety.

These include allegations that she is fearful for the

safety of herself and the children; that there was a

physical assault on her son, [DMG], on Sunday; that

there had been assaults several times in the past to

all three children as well as to herself; and that

she and her family were afraid of Dr. [G.] and that

he needs counsel; and that the matter should be

described as an emergency.

It is to be noted that at no time in the material

filed in Family Court or in her viva voce testimony

in court did she ever make any allegations of sexual

assault.  However, once proceedings were commenced to

set aside the ex parte order in the proceedings that

are now before me, such allegations were forthcoming.

I specifically find as a fact that all such

allegations are totally without foundation and are

made deliberately in order to gain custody of the

children of the marriage and to counter-balance her

obvious alcoholism.

[
9
]       I am not bound by the findings of fact made by
a

trial judge on an interim application.  I note, however,
that

Braidwood J. had the benefit of viva voce and affidavit

evidence.  There was a far more extensive body of
evidence

placed before him, relating to the conduct of the parties

leading up to separation and during the summer of 1994.

Because he had the benefit of examination and
cross-examination

of the parties and other critical witnesses, he was in as
good

a position as a trial judge on a final application.  In
such

circumstances his findings of fact cannot be ignored.

[
10
]      I have no hesitation in making similar findings
of

fact relating to the alleged physical and sexual abuse of
the

children.  There is not a scintilla of evidence to
support the

allegations made by TMG.  All of the evidence supports a

conclusion that AAG has been and continues to be a kind
and

loving parent to all three children.

[
11
]      On December 8, 1994, Braidwood J. made an order
for

supervised access by Mrs. G. in alternate weeks, three

hours for two visits and four hours for each visit thereafter.

The time for these visits has been increased and at
present

each visit can extend over a six hour period.

[
12
]      Interim spousal maintenance has been paid by
AAG

since the fall of 1994 in the amount of $3,500 per
month.  No

formal order has been entered with respect to that
maintenance

and consequently, there remains an issue between the
parties as

to whether payments received by TMG were to be net of
income

tax.  That matter will ultimately have to be resolved
with

Revenue Canada.  I note that on February 6, 1995 an
application

to increase interim maintenance was dismissed by
Braidwood J.

so that it does appear the amount paid by AAG as
maintenance

was with the approval of the court.

Supervised Access and Joint Guardianship

[
13
]      TMG seeks a variation of the current order
limiting

access and requiring that it be supervised.  She says
there is

no need for supervision and access should be liberal and

generous, designed to accommodate the busy schedules of
three

active children.

[
14
]      In support of her request, TMG called a number
of

persons to testify to her life in the community of
Qualicum

Beach, where she now resides.  She called friends and

acquaintances to say she was a responsible and loving
mother.

I have no difficulty in concluding that TMG loves her
children.

The difficulty is that many of her friends are unaware of
what

happened in the summer of 1994 and some remain convinced
that

AAG physically and sexually abused the children.  As they
had

not been informed of the content of the decision by
Braidwood

J., they appeared as her advocate because TMG has
persuaded

them she has done no wrong.  On the strength of her lies

concerning AAG's conduct, friends have loaned her money
to

assist in her legal battles.  Two of these people, upon

learning the truth, came to testify on behalf of AAG at
trial.

[
15
]      Dr. Ronald F. Braunstein is a Child Psychiatrist
and

he began medical treatment of RMG in October 1992.  In
the

first two sessions he met with RMG and her mother TMG.
All

three children attended the third session.  In this
initial

period he saw family members every two weeks.  RMG and
DMG had

treatment needs while SMG was symptom-free.  Dr.
Braunstein

continues to see all three children on a less frequent
basis.

Thus, he has been seeing the children for seven and
one-half

years, beginning a year and one-half before the
separation.

There is no doubt his evidence can be relied upon.

[
16
]      Dr. Braunstein testified that by October of
1993 he

became concerned with TMG's deteriorating parenting
skills.  In

January 1994 she discontinued her attendances with the

children.

[
17
]      Dr. Braunstein has prepared nine reports for
counsel

acting on behalf of AAG which have been filed in these

proceedings from time to time.  These reports are dated
June 1,

1994, July 7, 1994, November 8, 1994, December 20, 1994,

February 2, 1995, November 30, 1995, August 1, 1996, July
25,

1997 and December 28, 1997.  The court has relied upon
the

opinions expressed by Dr. Braunstein throughout these

proceedings.  He has consistently said that supervised
visits

were important and required for the protection of the
children.

He reports that there has been a steady positive progress
in

the development of the children.

[
18
]      Dr. Braunstein testified at trial.  He remains
of the

opinion that access by TMG is important for the children.
He

is equally firm in his recommendation that the access
continue

to be supervised.  He says there has been a loss of trust
in

their mother on the part of all three children.  They are
of

the view she does not tell the truth.  They know the

accusations of sexual and physical abuse made by their
mother

against their father were entirely untrue.  They are
aware of

their mother's attempts to destroy any relationship they
might

have enjoyed with their father.

[
19
]      Dr. Braunstein's opinion is that unsupervised
access

with TMG could potentially be very damaging for the
children.

He says the allegations made by TMG of sexual and
physical

abuse were extremely damaging to the children.  He notes
that

TMG continues to deny any part in the making of false

allegations.  She accepts no responsibility for the
damage that

her actions did to her children.  In the opinion of Dr.

Braunstein, it is essential that she address these issues
and

acknowledge that what she did was wrong.  Until that is
done,

she remains a potential threat to the continued
well-being of

her children.  Supervised access is a protection for the

children to ensure that her conduct does not cause a
setback in

the healthy growth of the children.

[
20
]      I agree with Dr. Braunstein.  TMG remains in
denial

concerning the impact her false allegations have had on
the

children.

[
21
]      TMG is an intelligent person.  She has a number
of

medical problems that have resulted in her being awarded
a

Canada Pension Plan disability benefit.  Her medical

conditions, as reported by her physician on the
application for

a disability pension, include:

1.  Back pain-degenerative disc disease at
L4-L5 and

to a lesser extent at L5-S1;

2.  Well differentiated follicular carcinoma of
the

thyroid.  She had surgery and radiation in
1996;

3.  Hypertension;

4.  Hiatus hernia; and,

5.  Hypomanic disorder.

[
22
]      It is to be noted that substance abuse, a serious

health problem and the apparent need for ongoing
appropriate

therapy were not listed by her family physician.

[
23
]      Because of her multiple medical conditions, she
is

considered eligible to receive pension benefits.  This
decision

will be reviewed in July 1999.

[
24
]      While she did not renew allegations of abuse at
this

trial, there is no doubt she has continued to make them
to her

friends and any other willing listener, right up to the
time of

the trial.  She now denies she has ever made such
allegations,

either before the interim hearing, at the interim hearing
or

after the interim judgment, a position that is not
credible.

It is not supported by the evidence.

[
25
]      Not until TMG was under cross-examination in
this

trial did she acknowledge AAG had not sexually abused the

children.  She was extremely reluctant to make that
concession,

all the while asserting that in some fashion she was not

responsible for the original complaint.  This is a good
example

of TMG's inability to acknowledge the truth when such an

acknowledgment might cast an unfavourable light on her
conduct.

[
26
]      TMG's unwarranted assertion concerning her
husband's

conduct caused damage to the children.  Because of her

continual refusal to admit her wrongdoing, the children
have

remained at risk.  Her relationship with the children
will

always be affected by events in the summer of 1994.  She
has no

hope of building a relationship of trust until she
acknowledges

to them that what she did to them and to AAG was wrong.

[
27
]      I have no confidence in relying on the evidence
of

TMG.  She did not tell the truth at all times during her

evidence and she is incapable of acknowledging her own
wrong-

doing.  She did not tell the truth when she said she had
not

continued to allege that AAG had physically and sexually
abused

the children, since the trial before Braidwood J.  She
did not

tell the truth about the extent of her use of alcohol and

marijuana.

[
28
]      TMG does appear to have a substance abuse
problem.

In that regard, she remains in denial.  Prior to
separation she

attended a treatment program in Minnesota.  In the course
of

treatment she acknowledged her dependency.  Upon her
return

home she failed to follow treatment recommendations and

continued to use alcohol and marijuana.  There were times
her

use was excessive.

[
29
]      While no definitive diagnosis has been made,
there

are suggestions that TMG has a personality disorder.  She
has

made no effort to seek assistance.  Any visits to
psychiatrists

or psychologists have not been for the purpose of
treatment but

solely to solicit their support in these proceedings.
She has

no insight into the disastrous financial situation her
family

now faces.  She is incapable of acknowledging her role
and the

significant part her conduct has had in creating that

situation.  She lives in a world of delusions, a world in
which

AAG is required to pay her substantial sums of money for
what

she considers her share of assets, together with lifelong

maintenance.

[
30
]      One example of her conduct that had serious
financial

consequences bears noting.  During the period in 1994
when she

enjoyed exclusive possession of the family home in West

Vancouver and exclusive possession of the Butterball
property

at Qualicum Beach, she moved almost all of the furniture
and

several fixtures from West Vancouver to Qualicum Beach.
The

move was entirely unnecessary.  She wreaked havoc on the
family

home in West Vancouver which was then undergoing
extensive

renovations.  Sinks and vanities were removed, leaving an

unsightly mess.  She caused a refrigerator to be moved,
leaving

damage marks on the floor.  The refrigerator was so large
it

could not have been used except in the place from which
it was

removed, a place specifically designed for its placement.

Braidwood J. was appalled at her conduct in removing
furniture

without notice or need.  He was apparently not told about
the

removal of fixtures or of the considerable damage left
behind.

AAG paid for both the move of the furniture from the home
and

the return of the furniture to the home, a total
exceeding

$16,000.  He also paid to have the damage repaired and
fixtures

reinstalled.  I am equally appalled by the conduct itself
and

the extravagance displayed by this conduct.

[
31
]      AAG is an ophthalmologist.  He has lived with
the

three children in the West Vancouver home since they were

returned to him in the late summer of 1994.  He is a
quiet,

thoughtful person and entirely believable.  Whenever the

evidence of TMG conflicts with his evidence, I reject her

evidence, preferring instead his recollection of events.

[
32
]      I have no confidence in TMG's parenting
abilities.

It was apparent over the course of this lengthy trial
that she

has no insight into her serious problems.  I accept the

opinions expressed by Dr. Braunstein and find that it
remains

in the best interests of the children that supervision of

access continue.  The children are attending a private
school

and doing very well.  Their social development is
appropriate.

The preliminary decisions made by the court to protect
the

children have proved, in the result, to be in their best

interests.  The evidence is insufficient to justify any
change

in the status quo.  I decline to make any changes in the

present access arrangements except to allow supervised

telephone contact, if convenient, on the occasion of a
birthday

or other special event.

[
33
]      It follows that this is not an appropriate case
in

which to make an order for joint guardianship and I
decline to

do so.  It is appropriate that TMG receive copies of the

children's report cards when they are received.  As well,
AAG

is to deliver an annual report, in writing, to TMG
outlining

any medical issues relating to the children.  If the
children

develop a medical condition that requires the attention
of a

doctor, AAG is to notify TMG in writing and provide the
name of

any attending physician.

[
34
]      The order restraining movement of the children
out of

the province is not necessary.  AAG has no intention of
leaving

this province.  The order of Dohm J. is to be varied to
delete

that restriction.

Division of Family Assets

[
35
]      On February 6, 1995, Braidwood J. dismissed a
motion

made by TMG for an advance of capital.  He concluded it
was not

clear she would receive capital, on the basis of the
financial

information at that time.  I find that at the time of

separation, liabilities exceeded the family assets; at
the time

of the s. 57 order, May 27, 1996, liabilities exceeded
the

family assets; and, at the time of the trial, liabilities

exceeded the family assets.  At each successive point in
time,

the situation had only worsened.  At all material times
it was

obvious there would be no assets to distribute and, in
each

year since separation, AAG has been on the edge of
bankruptcy.

[
36
]      Prior to separation, a decision was made to
renovate

the family home in West Vancouver.  This renovation of
the

family home placed a substantial drain on AAG's cash flow
and

he fell behind in the payment of his income taxes.  I
accept

the summary of taxes owing prepared for the purposes of
trial.

The income taxes presently owed are as follows:

Personal Income Taxes

Balance as at May 13, 1998
$370,353.09

(exclusive of interest and penalties)

$12,133.00

Taxes from the 1997 Corporate Return
40,976.00

Total
$98,624.00

[
37
]      Thus, AAG's income tax liabilities exceed
$500,000

and it is apparent, and has been for some time, that some

arrangement will have to be made with Revenue Canada if

bankruptcy proceedings are to be avoided.

[
38
]      At the time of marriage AAG had shares in the

Northmount Medical Centre.  These shares, now 2,000 in
number,

are owned by Dr. AAG Inc. and are taken into account in
the

valuation of the shares of that company.  This may not be
the

same number as AAG had at the time of marriage but he has
not

acquired any more since marriage.  He said that if the
numbers

differ it is because of changes in share structure.  The

company owns a medical building in North Vancouver and he

purchased his shares in 1980.  He does not recall having
any

debts or liabilities at the time of marriage.

[
39
]      TMG had an income of approximately $40,000 at
the

time of marriage but she was insolvent.  They had lived

together for a year and he had helped her out financially
until

her personal bankruptcy was inevitable.

[
40
]      In 1980, Argol Visual Contacts was incorporated
to

run the contact lens side of his practice.  His mother
was the

only shareholder and director.  As his practice is now

primarily a surgical practice, the company does little
contact

lens business.  It has provided a director's fee and
dividend

in the amount of $3,000 to $5,000 per year for his mother
and

it continues to do so.  TMG makes no claims against this

company.

[
41
]      In March 1987, AAG incorporated his
professional

practice, Dr. AAG Inc.  He holds all the common voting
shares

and he and TMG hold the common, non-voting shares.

[
42
]      In 1988 they purchased recreational property in

Qualicum for $200,000.  This was the Knight Terrace
property,

purchased with money that had been set aside for income
taxes.

The funds came from Dr. AAG Inc. and the property was

registered in the name of that company.  This turned out
to be

an error and so the company entered an agreement, on the
advice

of the accountant, whereby it held the property in trust
for

AAG.  TMG remained off title because of potential lingering

problems related to her earlier bankruptcy.

[
43
]      In 1984 AAG acquired two apartments in his
name.

These are Apartments 303 and 607-1508 Mariners Walk,
Vancouver.

Both were tax shelters.  Apartment 607 is furnished and
the

bank loan for the purchase of the furniture remains
outstanding

in the amount of $20,000.  There is a mortgage on each

property.  AAG pays interest of about $100 per month on
the

bank loan.  The Bank of Nova Scotia has a judgment
registered

against these properties.  There are also two charges
against

any interest TMG may have in these properties, one filed
by her

former solicitor and the other filed by a person who has
loaned

her money to finance this litigation.  I find the fair
market

value of Apt. 303 is $157,900 and Apt. 607 is $205,400.

[
44
]      In November 1991, a Family Trust was
established as

part of a fiscal reorganization.  AAG is the Trustee of
all of

the assets of the Trust and he has an uncontrolled
discretion

to decide on any dividends or payments from the trust to
the

beneficiaries.  The trust was established for the benefit
of

TMG, AAG and their children.  As part of the
reorganization,

the shares in Dr. AAG Inc. were then held by AAG and the
Family

Trust.

[
45
]      The second part of the reorganization took
place in

1992 when Argol Holdings Ltd. ("Argol") was
incorporated.  This

was incorporated as a holding company and it acquired all
of

the non-professional assets of Dr. AAG Inc.

[
46
]      In February 1992, the Knight Terrace property
in

Qualicum was transferred to AAG and TMG.  In order to
achieve

this purpose, Argol granted a housing loan in the amount
of

$205,629.  The reorganization was completed in May 1992.

[
47
]      In the fall of 1992, the Butterball property at

Qualicum Beach was acquired for $595,000.  There was a
vendor

mortgage back for $345,000 at 3% for six years, payable

interest only.  The principal is to be paid in the fall
of

1998.  The principal has been reduced by $15,000 since
the

purchase of the property.  There was a second mortgage to
the

Bank of Montreal for $242,000 and the balance was paid by
AAG.

This asset was purchased in his name as the trustee of
the

G. Family Trust.  I find the fair market value of this property

to be $420,000.

[
48
]      In January 1993, the Knight Terrace property
was sold

for $280,000 and the net proceeds used to pay taxes that
had

been reassessed from AAG's 1985 taxation year.  As the
proceeds

from the sale were not available to pay the housing loan
from

Argol, the loan was transferred and attributed to the

Butterball property.

[
49
]      In the fall of 1992, the renovations began on
the

West Vancouver property.  They were to cost about
$150,000 to

$200,000.  The project expanded, largely due to the
demands of

TMG, acquiesced in by AAG.  Ultimately, in excess of
$500,000

had been spent when renovations were completed after the

separation in 1994.  The renovations were paid from AAG's
cash

flow and money borrowed from the bank.  As a result, he
could

not pay his income taxes.  An additional housing loan was

recommended by his accountant as a method of deferring
taxes.

The new loan, when added to the existing housing loan on
the

Butterball property, brought the total of the housing
loans to

slightly in excess of $532,000.  The terms of these loans

require payment over a period of 20 years.  The loans are

currently in arrears.  As already noted, these housing
loans

are a tax deferral program.  If they are not paid there
will be

tax consequences for AAG.

[
50
]      The money advanced by the Bank of Montreal for
the

renovations of the West Vancouver family home and other
money

owed to the bank were rolled into a second mortgage on
that

property in the amount of $500,000.  AAG has been able to
pay

interest only on that debt and the whole of the principal

amount is owed to the bank.  There is, in addition, a
first

mortgage held by the bank in the amount of approximately

$158,000.  I find the fair market value of his property
to be

$800,000.

[
51
]      In the fall of 1992 and throughout 1993, AAG
and his

business partner caused the construction of Northmount
Eye

Surgical Centre.  Northmount Eye Surgical Ltd. was
incorporated

in October 1992 and is owned 50% by AAG and 50% by his
partner.

The construction of the surgical centre was paid for by a

single major supplier and the clinic opened in the fall
of

1993.  It consists of a reception area, two operating
rooms, a

pre-operative and a post-operative room.  The total cost
was

$700,000.  AAG and his partner guaranteed a total of
$100,000.

The plaintiff made no financial or other contribution to
the

construction of this facility.

[
52
]      W. A. McMann was qualified as a business
valuator.

He prepared a report dated November 7, 1996 and an
updated

report dated January 20, 1998.  I have no hesitation in

accepting the opinions expressed by Mr. McMann.  From his

reports, I conclude the corporate interests and share

[
53
]      Dr. AAG Inc. has been in a deficit position
since

1992.  Any intangible value, if it exists, is personal to
AAG

and, accordingly, has no fair market value.  The debts of
Dr.

AAG Inc. exceed its assets by $129,370.  I accept the
opinion

]      After separation and while there was a court ordered

funds held by either TMG or AAG.

]      I have used the most recent figures, but a

[
64
]      What is apparent from an analysis of assets and

liabilities at any point in time is that, at all material

times, the liabilities of this family constantly exceeded
its

assets.

[
65
]      Against that uncontradicted evidence, TMG
argues that

AAG should retain all the professional assets in his name
and

all of the debt.  He should be required to resolve all

outstanding income taxes for both of them.  She argues
she

should be paid $28,000 for her half interest in
Northmount

Surgical and half of the value of Argol ($351,130) paid
over 20

years.  With no evidence to support her request, she says
she

is entitled to be paid half of $183,000 for her interest
in Dr.

AAG Inc.  She then says the Qualicum Beach property
should be

remortgaged in October 1998 and the funds used for
repairs and

renovations.  Title to the property should then be held
through

the family trust for her benefit and the benefit of the
three

children.  She will assume the payment of 25% of the
mortgage

and taxes provided she receives adequate spousal
maintenance.

She says AAG should keep Apt. 303 and the West Vancouver

property.  Further, she says Apt. 607 should be conveyed
to her

and the children and that she will pay 25% of any
outstanding

mortgage.

[
66
]      I have not listed the entire requests made by
TMG.  I

record the foregoing to demonstrate how she has failed to
grasp

the seriousness of the current financial situation.  In her

argument, she chooses to ignore the staggering debt load,

preferring to say she is entitled to receive a half
interest in

most of the family assets, leaving the whole of the debt
to

AAG.  It is an argument that lacks a foundation in
reality.

[
67
]      I cannot ignore the fact that there are no
assets

left to distribute.  I regret this decision leaves TMG
heavily

in debt with no apparent ability to pay that debt.  On
the

evidence before me I can only conclude she has made a

significant contribution to her own misfortune.

[
68
]      AAG must be placed in a position where he can
reduce

the staggering debt load placed on this family and, if

possible, avoid personal bankruptcy.  To achieve this
end, I

make the following orders;

1.   All of the corporate assets are to be
transferred to

AAG.  TMG is to execute the requisite transfer

documents and if she fails to do so on demand,
the

transfers are to be made by order of the Court;

2.   The property at Qualicum Beach is to be sold
with the

net proceeds of sale deposited to the Family
Trust;

3.   Both apartments are to be sold and the net
proceeds

used to pay family liabilities.

4.   The West Vancouver property will remain in the
name

of AAG and there will be a declaration that TMG
has

no interest in this property;

5.   The RRSP money now held in trust is to be used
to

retire family liabilities;

6.   There will be a declaration that each of the
parties

is to pay the liabilities currently in their
own

names;

7.   TMG will retain all other assets in her name;
and,

8.   AAG will retain all other assets in his name.

Spousal Maintenance

[
69
]      AAG has a net income of approximately $240,000
per

annum.  He retains the services of a full-time nanny and
each

of the children attend private school.  He has had
mortgage

payments to maintain as well as the maintenance and
upkeep of

the real property assets.  Braidwood J. was unable to
quarrel

with the monthly expenditures set out in his property and

financial statement.  When I take into account the debt
he is

required to service, I, too, do not quarrel with the
monthly

expenditures he has enumerated.  In the end he reflects a

monthly deficit of almost $14,000.

[
70
]      TMG has been receiving $3,500 per month which
she

says is net of taxes.  She now seeks $6,000 per month,

retroactive to May 1996, upon which she would be required
to

pay her own income tax.  She is also in receipt of $874
per

month as a disability payment.

[
71
]      If the payment to TMG has been net of income
taxes,

AAG has a further liability with Revenue Canada.  The
only

comment I can make in that regard is that the figure did
appear

to have the approval of the Court even if there was no
formal

order.

[
72
]      Counsel for AAG says maintenance should be
fixed at

$3,000 per month.  She says TMG is capable of earning
income

and chooses not to work.

[
73
]      The receipt of a disability pension does not
mean the

recipient is unable to work.  People with far more
serious

disabilities work each day in an environment in which
their

disability is accommodated.  I make no comment on whether
TMG

is able to work.  She faces an uncertain period in her
life.

She will have to move from the Butterball property when
it is

sold and the issue of work cannot be addressed until she
has

relocated to new quarters.

[
74
]      In addition to the current maintenance payment
in the

amount of $3,500, TMG has been living free of any
accommodation

cost in the Butterball property.  She will continue to do
so

until it is sold.  In my view, there is no reason to
change the

present arrangements for maintenance.  There will be an
order

that AAG pay spousal maintenance in the amount of $3,500
per

month.  The matter can be revisited, if necessary, when
the

Butterball property has sold and AAG has had the
opportunity to

address the payment of current family liabilities.

Costs

[
75
]      In the ordinary course, AAG would be able to
recover

his costs of these proceedings.  Given the nature of the

unwarranted allegations and the conduct of TMG, it would
be

open to counsel to seek an order for special costs.
Counsel

for AAG, in her submissions on behalf of AAG, noted that
an

order for costs would be of no value to him, given the

financial circumstances of TMG.  Accordingly, I make no
order

for costs.  These proceedings have been extremely
contentious

and expensive and I have borne that fact in mind in
reaching

the conclusion that AAG must now be given the freedom to
deal

with family assets in a manner that allows him to remove
the

family from the present crushing debt load.
